# Emirates Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/emirates-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/emirates-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects flight data from emirates.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Emirates Flights with Python (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-emirates-flights)
- **Code:** [`emirates.py`](emirates.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Oneway](results/oneway.json) · [Roundtrip](results/roundtrip.json)

## What it scrapes

- Emirates.com flight search results (round-trip and one-way)
- Branded fare options per flight (SAVER, FLEX, etc.)
- Flight price, airline, departure/arrival times, stops, duration, layovers, cabin class, and seat availability
- Search-wide lowest fare

## Functions

- `scrape_flights(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date=None, locale='us/english')` → `FlightSearch`: Scrape flights from emirates.com

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`FarePrice`**: `amount`, `currency`
- **`FlightResult`**: `airline`, `flight_number`, `departure_time`, `departure_airport`, `arrival_time`, `arrival_airport`, `duration`, `stops`, `layovers`, `price`, `cabin_class`, `plane_model`, `fare_brand`, `seats_available`, `captured_at`
- **`FlightSearch`**: `locale`, `trip_type`, `origin`, `destination`, `route`, `search_date`, `departure_date`, `return_date?`, `lowest_fare`, `flights`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`emirates.py`](emirates.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Notes

Emirates.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking so this scraper is using Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature and browser rendering to capture the branded-fares API response.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/emirates-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_scrape_flights`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
